title: Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?
title_zh: LLM 驱动的智能体脚手架演化中，评估预算应投向何处？

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM)-driven agent scaffold evolution improves agent workflows through iterative candidate generation and evaluation. Evaluation both guides subsequent search and determines the final scaffold, but evaluating every candidate on the full task set incurs substantial execution costs. We investigate how evaluation budgets can be allocated across these two roles. Our experiments show that sparse feedback can sustain productive evolution, while additional targeted evaluation improves final selection. Replay analyses further show that shared informative items and a common scoring reference support comparisons among closely matched candidates. Motivated by these findings, we propose EvalAlloc , an evaluation allocation framework that combines sparse search-time feedback with targeted final confirmation. A short fully evaluated warm-up establishes a shared informative core and calibrates a response model whose item parameters remain fixed during search. After search, EvalAlloc refits the model and applies paired successive halving, reusing accumulated observations and executing only missing evaluations. Across four benchmarks and two evolution frameworks, EvalAlloc achieves higher mean performance than full evaluation in most settings while using approximately half as many evaluation cells.

paragraphs.en: A scaffold for a large language model (LLM) agent is an executable program that defines how an agent coordinates LLM calls, maintains intermediate state, and interacts with tools and external information sources ( Yao et al., 2023 ; Hu et al., 2025 ; Qin et al., 2024 ) . For Web-facing agents, scaffolds govern how agents acquire and use information through Web searches, document retrieval, and interactions with online services ( Nakano et al., 2021 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ) . While these scaffolds have traditionally been designed and refined manually, recent advances have enabled their automated optimization ( Hu et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ; Agrawal et al., 2026 ) . For example, ShinkaEvolve ( Lange et al., 2026 ) iteratively proposes scaffold modifications and uses evaluation feedback to guide subsequent evolution.
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体的脚手架是一种可执行程序，它定义了智能体如何协调 LLM 调用、维护中间状态，以及与工具和外部信息源交互（Yao et al., 2023；Hu et al., 2025；Qin et al., 2024）。 对于面向 Web 的智能体而言，脚手架决定了智能体如何通过 Web 搜索、文档检索以及与在线服务的交互来获取和使用信息（Nakano et al., 2021；Zhou et al., 2024）。 虽然这些脚手架传统上是由人工设计和改进的，但近期的进展已经使它们的自动化优化成为可能（Hu et al., 2025；Zhang et al., 2025；Agrawal et al., 2026）。 例如，ShinkaEvolve（Lange et al., 2026）迭代式地提出脚手架修改方案，并利用评估反馈来指导后续的进化。

paragraphs.en: However, evaluating candidate scaffolds can incur substantial execution costs. A single task instance may involve multiple LLM calls, retrieval steps, and tool interactions ( Mialon et al., 2024 ; Yao et al., 2025 ) , making full evaluation across many candidates expensive. Although parallel evaluation and asynchronous program generation can overlap computation ( Romera-Paredes et al., 2024 ) , feedback-dependent search decisions still require evaluation results. Existing approaches reduce evaluation costs through sparse score estimation and evaluation cascades ( Fisch et al., 2026 ; Gideoni et al., 2026 ) , treating evaluation primarily as a fitness-estimation problem. In scaffold evolution, however, evaluation supports two distinct decisions: it provides fitness feedback that shapes archive updates and subsequent proposals ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) , and it determines which scaffold is ultimately returned. These decisions impose different requirements: search benefits from inexpensive yet comparable feedback, whereas final selection requires reliable discrimination among competitive candidates. This raises a central question: How should a limited evaluation budget be allocated across these two decisions to improve the quality of the ultimately selected scaffold?
paragraphs.zh: 然而，评估候选脚手架可能带来高昂的执行成本。 单个任务实例可能涉及多次大语言模型调用、检索步骤和工具交互（Mialon et al., 2024; Yao et al., 2025），这使得在众多候选中进行全面评估的代价十分高昂。 尽管并行评估和异步程序生成可以重叠计算（Romera-Paredes et al., 2024），但依赖反馈的搜索决策仍然需要评估结果。 现有方法通过稀疏评分估计和评估级联来降低评估成本（Fisch et al., 2026; Gideoni et al., 2026），主要将评估视为一个适应度估计问题。 然而，在脚手架演化中，评估服务于两种不同的决策：它提供塑造档案更新和后续提议的适应度反馈（Zhang et al., 2026a），并且决定最终返回哪个脚手架。 这两种决策有不同的要求：搜索受益于廉价但可比较的反馈，而最终选择则需要在竞争性候选之间进行可靠的区分。 这引出了一个核心问题：应如何在这两种决策之间分配有限的评估预算，以提升最终被选中的脚手架的质量？

paragraphs.en: To answer this question, we investigate how evaluation allocation affects evolutionary search and final scaffold selection. Our investigation yields three findings. First, sparse evaluation feedback can sustain productive evolution, whereas removing feedback substantially degrades search quality. Second, shared informative items improve comparisons between closely matched candidates, while maintaining a common scoring reference helps preserve comparability across evolutionary iterations. Third, search improvements are concentrated in early iterations, whereas final selection remains sensitive to uncertainty among top candidates. These findings suggest that evaluation should provide inexpensive yet comparable feedback during search, while reserving additional observations for final selection.
paragraphs.zh: 为了回答这个问题，我们研究了评估分配如何影响进化搜索和最终的脚手架选择。 我们的研究得出了三个发现。 首先，稀疏的评估反馈能够维持有效的进化，而完全移除反馈则会显著降低搜索质量。 其次，共享的有信息量的条目可以改善 closely matched 候选者之间的比较，同时维持一个共同的评分参照有助于在进化迭代中保持可比性。 第三，搜索改进集中在早期迭代中，而最终选择对头部候选者之间的不确定性仍然敏感。 这些发现表明，评估应在搜索过程中提供廉价且具有可比性的反馈，同时将额外的观测保留给最终选择。

paragraphs.en: Motivated by these findings, we propose EvalAlloc , an evaluation allocation framework that separates sparse search-time feedback from targeted final selection. During search, a short fully evaluated warm-up identifies a shared informative core and calibrates a response model. Subsequent candidates are evaluated on sparse item sets centered on this core, while the model’s item parameters remain fixed to maintain a common scoring reference for archive updates and parent selection. After search, EvalAlloc applies warm-started paired successive halving (SH), reusing accumulated observations and performing only missing evaluations. A refitted response model further supports comparisons during later selection rounds. We evaluate EvalAlloc on four benchmarks and two evolution frameworks, with three independent runs per setting. Compared with full evaluation, EvalAlloc uses approximately half as many evaluation cells while achieving competitive or higher mean performance across the evaluated settings. Ablation studies further show that informative item allocation and final selection are the main contributors to its effectiveness. These results demonstrate the benefits of separating sparse search-time feedback from targeted final evaluation.

paragraphs.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows:
paragraphs.zh: 我们的主要贡献总结如下：

paragraphs.en: We investigate evaluation allocation as a decision-dependent problem in LLM-driven scaffold evolution, demonstrating that search-time feedback and final scaffold selection impose distinct requirements on evaluation resources.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将在由大语言模型驱动的脚手架演化中，将评估资源分配研究为一个依赖于决策的问题，证明搜索时反馈与最终脚手架选择对评估资源提出了不同的要求。

paragraphs.en: We propose EvalAlloc , an evaluation allocation framework that combines a shared informative core, a fixed search-time response model, and warm-started paired successive halving to allocate evaluation effort across evolutionary search and final selection.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 EvalAlloc，一个评估分配框架，它结合了共享信息核心、固定的搜索时响应模型以及热启动的成对逐次减半方法，以在进化搜索和最终选择之间分配评估资源。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate EvalAlloc across four benchmarks and two evolution frameworks, complemented by controlled replay analyses, demonstrating competitive final performance with substantially fewer evaluation cells.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在四个基准测试和两个演化框架上评估了 EvalAlloc，并辅以受控回放分析，结果表明其能以大幅更少的评估单元取得具有竞争力的最终性能。

paragraphs.en: LLM-Driven Agent and Program Evolution. Recent work has explored the automated design and optimization of agent scaffolds and executable workflows using LLMs ( Novikov et al., 2025 ) . ADAS ( Hu et al., 2025 ) uses a meta-agent to generate agent programs based on previous discoveries, while AFlow ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) employs Monte Carlo Tree Search to optimize code-represented workflows. Other approaches, including ShinkaEvolve ( Lange et al., 2026 ) and AdaEvolve ( Cemri et al., 2026 ) , iteratively generate, evaluate, and refine programs using evaluation feedback to guide subsequent search. These approaches primarily focus on improving candidate generation and evolutionary optimization. Our work instead examines the evaluation process underlying this feedback-driven search, studying how limited evaluation resources can support both evolutionary decisions and final scaffold selection.

sents.en: Other approaches, including ShinkaEvolve ( Lange et al., 2026 ) and AdaEvolve ( Cemri et al., 2026 ) , iteratively generate, evaluate, and refine programs using evaluation feedback to guide subsequent search.
sents.zh: 其他方法，包括 ShinkaEvolve（Lange 等，2026）和 AdaEvolve（Cemri 等，2026），利用评估反馈来指导后续搜索，迭代地生成、评估和改进程序。

sents.en: These approaches primarily focus on improving candidate generation and evolutionary optimization.
sents.zh: 这些方法主要聚焦于改进候选生成和演化优化。

sents.en: Our work instead examines the evaluation process underlying this feedback-driven search, studying how limited evaluation resources can support both evolutionary decisions and final scaffold selection.
sents.zh: 我们的工作则考察这种反馈驱动搜索背后的评估过程，研究有限的评估资源如何能同时支持演化决策和最终脚手架选择。

paragraphs.en: Efficient LLM Evaluation. Reducing the cost of evaluating LLMs has received growing attention. Methods such as tinyBenchmarks ( Polo et al., 2024 ) use carefully selected examples and statistical estimation to approximate full-benchmark performance, while SparseEval ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) optimizes representative items for efficient score estimation and ranking. CollabEval ( Fisch et al., 2026 ) exploits shared information across evaluations through matrix completion to improve statistical efficiency. Growing Pains ( Habba et al., 2026 ) uses fixed item-response calibration and anchor items to maintain score comparability across evaluation periods. These studies demonstrate the effectiveness of sparse observations and response modeling. However, in scaffold evolution, evaluation estimates also influence archive updates and subsequent candidate generation. Therefore, we examine not only estimation accuracy, but also how shared informative observations and stable scoring references support reliable evolutionary decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 高效的LLM评估。 降低LLM评估成本已受到越来越多的关注。 tinyBenchmarks（Polo et al., 2024）等方法使用精心挑选的样例和统计估计来近似完整基准的性能，而SparseEval（Zhang et al., 2026b）则优化代表性题目以实现高效的分数估计与排名。 CollabEval（Fisch et al., 2026）通过矩阵补全利用跨评估的共享信息，以提高统计效率。 Growing Pains（Habba et al., 2026）使用固定的题目-作答校准和锚定题目，以保持跨评估周期的分数可比性。 这些研究证明了稀疏观测与作答建模的有效性。 然而，在脚手架演化中，评估估计还会影响存档更新和后续候选生成。 因此，我们不仅考察估计精度，还考察共享的有信息观测和稳定的评分参照如何支持可靠的演化决策。

paragraphs.en: Evaluation Allocation and Candidate Selection. Evaluation allocation is closely related to sequential resource allocation and best-arm identification. Successive halving ( Jamieson and Talwalkar, 2016 ) and Hyperband ( Li et al., 2018 ) progressively concentrate evaluation resources on promising candidates, while racing-based methods such as irace ( López-Ibáñez et al., 2016 ) eliminate weaker configurations through sequential comparisons. Common random numbers ( Glasserman and Yao, 1992 ) provide a classical motivation for evaluating alternatives under shared conditions to reduce the variance of pairwise comparisons. Recent analyses of code evolution ( Gideoni et al., 2026 ) also highlight the importance of reliable candidate evaluation and selection. Building on these ideas, our work studies evaluation allocation across two distinct stages: providing inexpensive yet comparable feedback during evolution and reusing accumulated observations for reliable final scaffold selection.
paragraphs.zh: 评估分配与候选选择。 评估分配与序贯资源分配以及最优臂识别密切相关。 连续减半（Successive halving）（Jamieson and Talwalkar, 2016）和 Hyperband（Li et al., 2018）逐步将评估资源集中于有前景的候选，而基于竞赛的方法（如 irace（López-Ibáñez et al., 2016））则通过序贯比较淘汰较弱的配置。 公共随机数（Glasserman and Yao, 1992）为在共享条件下评估各备选项以降低成对比较的方差提供了经典动机。 近期关于代码演化的分析（Gideoni et al., 2026）也强调了可靠的候选评估与选择的重要性。 在这些思想的基础上，我们的工作研究跨两个不同阶段的评估分配：在演化过程中提供廉价但可比较的反馈，并复用积累的观测以实现可靠的最终脚手架选择。

paragraphs.en: We study four benchmarks: HotpotQA ( Yang et al., 2018 ) , HoVer ( Jiang et al., 2020 ) , DROP ( Dua et al., 2019 ) , and IFBench ( Pyatkin et al., 2026 ) . paragraphs.en: Most analyses in this section replay evaluators on the 24 Full runs (four benchmarks, two frameworks, three seeds), in which every candidate is evaluated on all SEARCH items, so the full-SEARCH mean of each candidate is known. A replay keeps the candidate sequence fixed and varies only which cells the evaluator observes. We measure two search-time quantities. Close-pair agreement is the share of candidate pairs whose full-SEARCH means differ by at most .03 that the evaluator orders correctly; these are the comparisons that archive updates face. Archive regret is, averaged over the run, the gap between the mean full-SEARCH score of the ten best candidates generated so far and that of the ten candidates the evaluator ranks highest.

paragraphs.en: Final scaffold selection requires more reliable comparisons than those needed to guide evolutionary search. Figure 2 compares the native selection rule with successive halving (SH) on the same candidate pools under different search-time evaluation strategies. paragraphs.en: Figure 3 illustrates EvalAlloc , an evaluation allocation framework that distributes evaluation effort across three stages: Core Calibration , Shared-Core Evolution , and Warm-Started Selection . EvalAlloc decouples the two roles of evaluation: search-time feedback only needs to be cheap and comparable enough to guide evolution, whereas the final choice needs precise comparisons among the strongest candidates. It therefore splits one evaluation budget into a sparse search stage and a separate selection stage that reuses every observation collected during search. The key idea is to invest a small evaluation budget upfront to establish a reusable reference, use shared informative items to provide comparable feedback throughout evolution, and concentrate additional evaluations on final scaffold selection. EvalAlloc operates as a drop-in evaluator, leaving the native framework’s proposal, archive, and parent-selection policies unchanged.
paragraphs.zh: 图3展示了EvalAlloc，一个将评估工作分配到三个阶段的评估分配框架：核心校准（Core Calibration）、共享核心演化（Shared-Core Evolution）和热启动选择（Warm-Started Selection）。 EvalAlloc将评估的两种角色解耦：搜索时的反馈只需足够廉价且具有可比性，以引导演化；而最终选择则需要在最强的候选者之间进行精确比较。 因此，它将一份评估预算拆分为一个稀疏的搜索阶段和一个独立的选择阶段，后者会复用搜索期间收集到的所有观测结果。 其核心思想是：预先投入少量评估预算来建立一个可复用的参照，利用共享的高信息量条目在整个演化过程中提供可比较的反馈，并将额外的评估集中在最终的智能体框架（scaffold）选择上。 EvalAlloc以即插即用的评估器方式运行，不改变原生框架的提案、存档和父代选择策略。

paragraphs.en: Baselines. We compare EvalAlloc against five evaluation strategies with different budget allocations. Skip Eval performs no evaluation during either search or final selection, and select the last valid evolved program. Successive Halving (SH) ( Jamieson and Talwalkar, 2016 ) provides no evaluation feedback during search and applies successive halving to the generated candidate pool for final selection. Random evaluates each candidate on a randomly sampled 50% subset of SEARCH items. Cascade ( Novikov et al., 2025 ; Agrawal et al., 2026 ) first evaluates candidates on 20% of SEARCH items and promotes candidates meeting a top-25% threshold to full evaluation, while allocating no additional evaluations to the remaining candidates. Full evaluates every candidate on all SEARCH items.
paragraphs.zh: 基线方法。 我们将 EvalAlloc 与五种采用不同预算分配方式的评估策略进行比较。 Skip Eval 在搜索和最终选择阶段均不进行任何评估，并选择最后一个有效的进化程序。 Successive Halving（SH）（Jamieson and Talwalkar, 2016）在搜索过程中不提供任何评估反馈，并对生成的候选池应用逐次减半方法进行最终选择。 Random 在随机抽取的 50% 的 SEARCH 项目子集上评估每个候选。 Cascade（Novikov et al., 2025；Agrawal et al., 2026）首先在 20% 的 SEARCH 项目上评估候选，将达到前 25% 阈值的候选提升至完整评估，而不为其余候选分配额外的评估。 Full 在所有 SEARCH 项目上评估每个候选。

paragraphs.en: Table 3 compares the TEST performance and evaluation cost of different strategies. Across both evolution frameworks and all four benchmarks, EvalAlloc matches or slightly exceeds the mean TEST score of Full while using approximately half as many evaluation cells. It also outperforms Random and Cascade in cross-benchmark average performance at comparable or lower evaluation cost. These results demonstrate that allocating evaluations selectively can provide a better cost–performance tradeoff than uniformly evaluating candidates. The evaluation costs differ between the two frameworks partly due to their handling of invalid proposals. AdaEvolve retries program generation when a proposal is invalid, whereas ShinkaEvolve discards invalid proposals without replacement. Since invalid programs incur no evaluation cost, ShinkaEvolve evaluates fewer valid candidates, resulting in lower realized evaluation costs, particularly under Full evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 表3比较了不同策略的TEST性能与评估成本。 在两个演化框架和全部四个基准上，EvalAlloc在仅使用约一半评估单元格的情况下，匹配或略微超过Full的平均TEST分数。 在相近或更低的评估成本下，它还在跨基准平均性能上优于Random和Cascade。 这些结果表明，有选择地分配评估能够比统一评估候选方案提供更好的成本—性能权衡。 两个框架之间的评估成本存在差异，部分原因在于它们对无效提案的处理方式不同。 当提案无效时，AdaEvolve会重试程序生成，而ShinkaEvolve则直接丢弃无效提案且不做替换。 由于无效程序不产生评估成本，ShinkaEvolve评估的有效候选方案更少，导致实际评估成本更低，在Full评估下尤为明显。

paragraphs.en: Table 4 shows that removing final confirmation consistently reduces TEST performance, highlighting the importance of additional evaluation for selecting among competitive candidates. Replacing informative items with random ones produces the largest average degradation, suggesting that sharing evaluation items alone is insufficient without considering their informativeness. Removing the response model has a smaller and less consistent effect, as the shared core already provides substantial comparability among candidates. paragraphs.en: To examine this discrepancy without confounding differences in search trajectories, we analyze the fully evaluated candidate pools from the Full runs. Higher-scoring candidates tend to consume more tokens per item, with average within-run Spearman correlations of 0.25 and 0.36 for ShinkaEvolve and AdaEvolve, respectively. Likewise, the 60 items with the highest response variability consume 1.08 and 1.13 times the average tokens per item. paragraphs.en: Evaluation influences both evolutionary search and final scaffold selection. Our investigation shows that sparse informative feedback can guide evolution, while shared evaluation items and a stable scoring reference support comparable decisions across candidates. Motivated by these findings, we propose EvalAlloc , which combines sparse search-time feedback with warm-started final confirmation. Across four benchmarks and two evolution frameworks, EvalAlloc achieves competitive performance while using approximately half as many evaluation cells as Full. These results highlight the importance of allocating evaluation effort according to its distinct roles in search and final selection.
